analysis.title: Forget AI, Goldman says it's time to get a life
key_insights: Goldman Sachs flags the experience economy as an interesting trade into earnings season. Real US spending on experiences grew almost 6% y/y in Q1 2026 versus about 1% a year earlier, while broader services spending grew only about 2%.
Goldman's Consumer Experiences basket has underperformed the S&P 500 ex-AI index by roughly 14%, despite the acceleration in underlying demand.
Forward earnings expectations for the basket have kept rising while share prices have fallen from their summer highs, which widens the gap between fundamentals and performance.
Relative to the equal-weighted S&P 500, the median experience stock trades near the bottom of its 10-year valuation range.

Experience stocks have recently shown a negative correlation with AI. Goldman argues the correlation could turn positive, because more time spent with machines may raise the value of physical and social experiences.
Hedge funds have started rebuilding exposure to experience stocks, but positioning remains well below previous peaks, so the trade is not crowded.

Company datapoints show strong demand: Live Nation fan growth above 10%, Sphere Entertainment 3.6 million tickets and $450 million from The Wizard of Oz, Marriott US and Canada luxury RevPAR up more than 9%, and Viking 96% booked for 2026 with 53% of 2027 sold.
Disney, Formula 1 and other live entertainment operators are reported to be seeing similarly resilient demand.

Stated risks are higher oil prices hurting travel economics and discretionary spending vulnerability to a weaker consumer. Goldman argues exposure to wealthier consumers, improving earnings revisions and light positioning offer some insulation and upside.

sector_views.rationale: Goldman sees accelerating experience spending, rising forward earnings, valuations near 10-year lows relative to the equal-weighted S&P 500, and light hedge fund positioning.

earnings_insights: Live Nation: fan growth exceeding 10%, with no signs of consumer weakness (company commentary as cited, period not specified).
Sphere Entertainment: 3.6 million tickets sold and $450 million generated by The Wizard of Oz (reported figures as cited, no period given).
Marriott: luxury revenue per available room up more than 9% in the US and Canada (reported, period not specified).
Viking: 96% booked for 2026 and 53% of 2027 sold (company-reported booking status, date not specified).
Forward earnings expectations for Goldman's Consumer Experiences basket have continued to climb (estimate revisions, not a reported print).

macro_indicators.interpretation: Experience spending is accelerating from about 1% a year earlier, ahead of broader services spending.
Services spending overall is growing more slowly than experiences.
